newsitem.title: USA: Many abused girls are maltreated as adults - study.
newsitem.headline: Many abused girls are maltreated as adults - study.

text.p: Half of women who were abused as children were maltreated as adults, and many victims of domestic violence do not seek help to ease a troublesome relationship, new studies said on Tuesday.
Researchers at The Johns Hopkins School of Medicine in Baltimore found 22 percent of 1,931 women surveyed experienced childhood physical or sexual abuse.

Of those abused as children, half reported being abused as adults. Those abused as children but not as adults suffered higher rates of depression, anxiety, low self-esteem, drug abuse, and were more likely to have attempted suicide.

"In this study, it made little difference whether the abuse was sexual or physical...(The) 'wounds' of childhood may go unhealed," study author Jeanne McCauley wrote in the Journal of the American Medical Association.
Researchers at Methodist Hospital in Memphis, Tennessee, looked at 62 episodes of domestic violence and found that only 12 victims reported having sought medical care, counselling or shelter.

"One barrier to seeking help that victims mentioned was the prospect that seeking care or assistance in the prosecution of their assailants would escalate the violence," author Daniel Brookoff of the Memphis hospital wrote in the Journal.

To help emergency room hospital staff discern the victims of abuse, a team from the Denver Health Medical Centre devised three simple questions that located nearly three-quarters of the abuse victims found by more in-depth questioners.

The questions concerned whether the person had been physically hurt by someone in the past year, whether they felt safe in their current relationship, and whether there was a partner from a previous relationship who made them feel unsafe now.
